title: Michelle Young:
title_q: “Confidence Grows in Front of Your Face”
headline: Sneakers decide which kids get to play. Michelle watched shy kids light up when they got a new pair.
story: Michelle Young runs Homework and Hoops, an after-school program with tutoring and basketball. She says it plainly: sneakers are a big reason some kids cannot play sports. It looks like a small thing. It is not.

At the Mall of America she watched kids walk in shy and walk out running in new sneakers. You can see the confidence grow in front of your face. Keep it bright and happy. This is the only Mall of America cut about sports.
do: Open on her face with the hook text on frame 1: <q>No sneakers. No team.</q>
Cut tight between bites. Small punch-ins (up to 120%) hide the jumps.
Keep captions on screen the whole time, big and readable.
End on her smile after “really joyful”.
dont: No logo, fade or name card at 0:00.
No stock footage, no invented shots. Michelle on camera only.
Don't use 030_3167.MXF. Those are her “Are You Happy?” answers, saved for another video.
Don't use sports or “Homework and Hoops” lines in any other Mall of America cut.

voice.quote: Sneakers are a huge part of why sometimes students aren't able to partake in sports.

rows.sfx: Room tone only. No whoosh on frame 1.
rows.music: Upbeat bed starts on frame 1, low, under her voice.

rows.frame_alt: Michelle talking, hands folded on her knee

rows.motion: Hook text off on the cut. Captions only.

voice.quote: I currently run a program called Homework and Hoops, where we do after-school tutoring with math and literacy, but then also give the students a chance to play basketball.

rows.frame_alt: Michelle with hands together in front of her chest
rows.visual: Back to 100%. Her hands move with the words.

voice.quote: It's such a huge part, even though it seems like such a small thing that a lot of times people take for granted.

rows.visual: Michelle on camera. Start at “The moment”. Cut “yeah, moments or” before it. We have no picture of the kids. Do not use stock.

voice.quote: The moment that has stuck with me today is watching the students come in. They're a little bit timid, they're shy, they're not really sure what's going on, and they sit down in the chair and you can see them start to light up.

rows.visual: Long bite (16 s). Punch in to 110% on “whether they're the Nikes” to break it. Back to 100% on “they're just so confident”.
rows.motion: Captions only. Spell the brands right: Nikes, Puma, Jordan.

voice.quote: So many of them came in, you know, with whatever sneakers that they had, and by the end they're running around with their new sneakers on, whether they're lighting up, whether they're the Nikes, whether they're Puma, Jordan, whatever it is, they're just so confident and they're so happy and they're so excited.

rows.frame_alt: Michelle talking to the lens, hands open
rows.visual: Straight on her face. Hold 0.5 s after “joyful”, then cut to the end card.

voice.quote: And to be able to see that change and see the confidence grow in front of your face has just been really joyful.
